title: Torque a busbar lug bolt with a click-type torque wrench
instruction: Torque the lug bolt with the torque wrench on it. The wrench is already set to the bolt's torque. Then let go.
context: Electricians and panel builders torque lug and terminal bolts to the value marked on the device with a calibrated torque tool; the US electrical code (NEC 110.14(D)) has required one where a value is marked since 2017. Click-wrench instructions say: pull steadily at the grip and stop the moment the wrench clicks. The wrench does not limit torque, it only signals it: pulling on through the click keeps tightening, past the joint's +10 % tolerance, and an over-torqued screw stretches or the lug cracks; pulling through scores 0. The ability tested: stop a steady pull on a one-shot signal from the tool (the detent breaking over in a 6 deg kink), when nothing about the bolt says stop and nothing stops the pull. Done by: electricians (about 780,000 US) and electrical equipment assemblers (O*NET 47-2111.00, 51-2022.00).
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the arm bases (x forward, y left). The joint: a copper flat bar 20 x 6 mm, 12 cm long, on two glass-polyester standoff insulators 2.4 cm tall, runs from x 30 to 42 at y -9. On it, a tinned-copper tube lug for 16 mm2 (about 6 AWG) cable with an M5 hole (palm 18 x 12 x 3 mm, barrel 8 mm across), its cable (black PVC, 8 mm over the insulation) leading off forward. The bolt: M5 x 0.8 x 16 mm hex, class 8.8 zinc-plated steel, 8 mm across flats, with a flat washer; vertical at x 33, y -9, through the lug and bar into an M5 self-clinching nut in the bar. The lug and the panel label are marked 3 N*m (the label is not modelled). The bolt starts snug, at 1.5 N*m (README). The tool: an adjustable click-type torque wrench (chrome-vanadium steel, 1/4-inch square drive, 2-10 N*m range, ISO 6789 Type II class A, +/-6 %), 26 cm long, set to 3 N*m. Under its drive, an inline rotary torque transducer (26 x 26 mm, 4 cm tall), then an 8 mm socket on the bolt head. The wrench lies flat, 9.7 cm above the table: head, transducer and socket (300 g) turn with the bolt; the handle (100 g, 14 x 12 mm tube) is on a pivot in the head 4.5 cm from the bolt, held in line by a sprung detent; black rubber grip, 7 cm long, 18 x 18 mm, its load mark 21.5 cm from the bolt, so 3 N*m takes 14 N there. The handle points toward the right arm (-y); tightening pulls the grip toward the robot. Sim only (real trials score from the transducer): 100 % of the set torque at 4.9 deg past snug, 110 % at 5.9 deg, yield at 230 % (17.7 deg); the sim's torques are 1/7 of the real ones (the wrench clicks at 2 N at the grip).
scoring: Peak torque P, in % of the set torque: on a real rig, the transducer's peak-hold reading (100 % = 3 N*m); in the sim, from the bolt's tightest turn past snug (100 % at 4.9 deg, 110 % at 5.9 deg). Clicked: the detent broke over (handle bent 1.5 deg on its pivot). Fail, latched for the trial (score 0): P over 110 % (over 3.3 N*m: pulled on through the click; the bolt yields at 230 %), or the bolt turned back more than 3 deg from its tightest. Score: 1.0 for torqued in tolerance: clicked, P 90-110 % (2.7-3.3 N*m) and the bolt still within 1 deg of its tightest; otherwise 0.25 if the bolt is at least 1.5 deg past snug (P at least 65 %: under-torqued); else 0. Halved unless both grippers are at least 10 cm outside the wrench's bounding box and the bolt and grip are still (under 0.05 deg and 0.3 mm per control step). 1.0 is success, held for 1 s. Real rig: angles from the transducer's angle channel, from the snug paint mark. Scored at the last step. Possible scores: 0, 0.125, 0.25, 0.5, 1.0.
reset_notes: Back the bolt off (fit a new bolt if its peak went over 110 %); run it down by hand, then to 1.5 N*m on the transducer, and paint-mark the head and lug; check the wrench is set to 3 N*m and fit it on the bolt in line, the handle pointing toward the right arm.
fidelity: Rigid boxes, one shared friction (1.2/1.0). The bolt is a hinge with Coulomb friction; a per-step rule raises it with the turn (clamp-up, angles estimated from the M5 joint's stiffness), flat past the yield. Torques are 1/7 of the real 3 N*m joint's (2 N at the grip, not 14 N) for the soft sim arm. The detent is a sprung hinge; a per-step rule drops it to a light reset spring at 1.5 deg (break-over), the handle swings to a 6 deg stop and re-arms within 0.5 deg. The ratchet is not modelled.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0; demo: 1.0 (the hand lets go, lifts and moves over 10 cm clear of the wrench before the 1 s success hold)
